styles.name: Tangle-Free Brushing
styles.description: The foundation skill. Done right it takes two minutes and causes no pain.
styles.oneLiner: The two minutes every style begins with
styles.herJob: She's in charge of the spray bottle. One mist when you ask.
styles.commonFailure: She winces and pulls away, usually because the comb hit an uncleared knot higher up before the ends were free.
styles.theFix: Stop, move your anchor hand back to the halfway point, and restart from the ends. Never move the anchor hand higher until the comb passes freely below it.

steps.title: Pick the right tool
steps.instruction: If her hair is tangled, use the wide-tooth comb throughout. Only swap to the soft brush at the very end, once the comb runs through easily.
steps.endState: You're holding the comb and she's sitting in front of you.
steps.why: Using a brush on a knot does not smooth it. It pulls hair out.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, not dripping, and smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers. Work in sections, ends first, fingers then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section, root to tip.

steps.title: Set your anchor hand
steps.instruction: Put your free hand around her hair about halfway down. Hold it firmly without squeezing. This hand acts as a shield to stop the pulling.
steps.endState: The hair below your hand hangs loose.
steps.why: This stops any tugging force from reaching her scalp.

steps.title: Clear the ends first
steps.instruction: Start the comb 5 cm above the ends and pull down. If it catches, use shorter strokes on that bit until it runs free. Never force through a knot.
steps.withHer: Ask her to tell you when it pulls.
steps.endState: The comb runs freely through the last 5 cm.

curly.title: Clear the ends first
curly.instruction: Work the ends of one section at a time. Fingers first until they slide through, then follow with the wide-tooth comb over the same bit. Mist again if a section is drying out before you reach it.
curly.endState: The comb runs freely through the ends of the section you're on.

steps.title: Work upward in stages
steps.instruction: Move your hand up 5 cm to anchor the hair higher up. Comb down through everything below your hand. When that runs free, move your hand and comb up again. Repeat until you reach the scalp.
steps.endState: One smooth stroke from top to bottom.

curly.title: Work upward in stages
curly.instruction: Move up the same section, fingers first then the comb, a little at a time. When one section runs free, twist it loosely out of the way and move to the next.
curly.endState: Each section runs free from root to tip before you move to the next.

steps.title: Smooth with the brush
steps.instruction: Swap to the soft brush. Starting above her forehead, brush in long firm strokes down to the ends. Do the whole head: both sides, top and back.
steps.endState: The hair lies flat and looks shiny.

curly.title: Shape with your fingertips
curly.instruction: Skip the brush. Shape each section with your fingertips, and mist lightly again if it's looking dry rather than reaching for the comb.
curly.endState: The curls look soft and defined, not flattened or frizzed.

styles.name: Classic Ponytail
styles.description: All hair gathered and secured at the back of the head, level with the tops of the ears.
styles.herJob: She wears the elastic on her wrist until you need it.
styles.commonFailure: A ridge or bump across the top of the head where the two hand-sweeps met.
styles.theFix: Undo the elastic. Regather by starting from the hairline at the forehead with both hands and sweeping all the way back in one continuous motion before your hands meet.

steps.title: Detangle first
steps.instruction: Comb through from the ends up, holding the hair halfway down with your free hand so you don't tug. Don't move on until it runs clean.
steps.endState: No catching from top to bottom.
steps.why: This stops any pulling reaching her scalp.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, not dripping, and smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers. Work in sections, ends first, fingers then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section, root to tip.

steps.title: Gather the hair
steps.instruction: Gather the hair. Put both hands flat against the sides of her head above her ears. Sweep all the hair straight back until your hands meet. Hold the bundle firmly in one hand.
steps.endState: One clean bundle at the back. No loose strands in front of her ears.

curly.title: Gather the hair
curly.instruction: Gather the hair. Put both hands flat against the sides of her head above her ears. Gather it back loosely, without dragging at the hairline, until your hands meet. Hold the bundle firmly in one hand.
curly.endState: One clean bundle at the back, with the hairline soft, not pulled tight.

steps.title: Set the height
steps.instruction: Slide your holding hand up or down the back of her head until it's level with the tops of her ears. Check by touching the top of one ear with your free hand.
steps.withHer: Ask her to look straight ahead.
steps.endState: The bundle is centred and level with the tops of her ears.

steps.title: Smooth the surface
steps.instruction: Smooth the surface. Use a soft brush to stroke from her forehead and above each ear straight back toward your holding hand. Keep your grip firm so you don't lose the hair.
steps.endState: Flat and bump-free all the way around her head.

curly.title: Smooth the surface
curly.instruction: Smooth the surface. Use your fingertips, not a brush, to smooth the hair above her forehead and each ear back toward your holding hand. Mist lightly again if a section is frizzing, rather than brushing it flatter.
curly.endState: Flat and bump-free all the way round her head, with the curl pattern still intact.

steps.title: Secure with the elastic
steps.instruction: Secure the ponytail. Loop the elastic over the bundle, twist it into a figure-eight, and loop it again. Aim for three loops minimum.
steps.endState: It doesn't move when she shakes her head.

steps.title: Double check the tension
steps.instruction: Slide two fingers under the elastic at the back of her head.
steps.withHer: Ask her if it pulls anywhere.
steps.endState: Two fingers can slide under the elastic without forcing it.

styles.name: High Ponytail
styles.description: All hair gathered at the very top of her head, giving more height and keeping the neck completely clear.
styles.herJob: She counts the loops out loud. Stop at three.
styles.commonFailure: The ponytail leans to one side.
styles.theFix: Undo and regather. Before securing, stand directly behind her and look down from above to check the bundle is centred. A mirror in front of her also lets you check from the front.

steps.title: Detangle first
steps.instruction: Comb through from the ends up, holding the hair halfway down with your free hand so you don't tug.
steps.endState: No catching from top to bottom.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, not dripping, and smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers. Work in sections, ends first, fingers then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section, root to tip.

steps.title: Gather upward to the very top of her head
steps.instruction: Gather the hair. Place your hands flat against the sides of her head above her ears. Sweep all the hair upward to the very top of her head. Hold the bundle firmly in one hand.
steps.withHer: Ask her to keep her head still.
steps.endState: The hair is gathered at the highest point of her head.

curly.title: Gather upward to the very top of her head
curly.instruction: Gather the hair. Place your hands flat against the sides of her head above her ears. Gather it upward toward the crown, easing it up rather than dragging the hairline tight. Hold the bundle firmly in one hand.
curly.endState: The hair is gathered at the crown, with the hairline soft, not strained.

steps.title: Check the position
steps.instruction: Position the ponytail. Ensure the bundle sits right at the top of her crown. Move your hand to correct it before reaching for the elastic.
steps.endState: Centred at the top, not sagging backward.

curly.title: Check the position
curly.instruction: Position the ponytail at the crown, not dragged further forward or pulled tighter to get it there.
curly.endState: Sits at the crown with the hairline soft, not strained.

steps.title: Smooth the surface
steps.instruction: Smooth the surface. Take the soft brush. Brush upward from her forehead and from above each ear straight toward your holding hand. Keep your grip firm.
steps.endState: Both sides and front are flat, running smoothly upward without any bumps.

curly.title: Smooth the surface
curly.instruction: Smooth the surface. Use your fingertips, not a brush, from her forehead and above each ear toward your holding hand.
curly.endState: Both sides and front are smooth and flat, without any pulling at the hairline.

steps.title: Secure firmly
steps.instruction: Secure the bundle. Loop the elastic round at least four times. Ask her after the third wrap whether it feels tight.
steps.endState: The fourth loop is snug, not sore.
steps.why: The extra height creates more pull than a mid-height ponytail and needs more holding.

steps.title: Final inspection
steps.instruction: Ask her to nod, then shake her head, while you watch the ponytail from behind.
steps.withHer: Ask her if it pulls anywhere.
steps.endState: The ponytail points upward and doesn't droop or shift when she moves.

styles.name: Two Even Bunches
styles.description: Hair divided down the middle and gathered into one ponytail on each side, level with the ears.
styles.herJob: She checks they match in the mirror.
styles.commonFailure: One bunch ends up higher or thicker than the other.
styles.theFix: Check from the front before calling it done. A small height difference is easy to fix by removing the elastic from the lower bunch and resecuring half a centimetre higher.

steps.title: Detangle all the hair
steps.instruction: Comb it all through before you touch the parting.
steps.endState: Runs freely everywhere.
steps.why: Both sides need to start from smooth hair or the parting will look uneven.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, not dripping, and smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers. Work in sections, ends first, fingers then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section, root to tip.

steps.title: Draw the centre parting
steps.instruction: Put the pointed end of the tail comb where her hair starts, in the middle above her nose. Draw it straight back to the middle of the back of her neck. Go slowly, lining it up with her nose from the front.
steps.endState: Roughly equal hair each side.

steps.title: Move one side clear
steps.instruction: Lay all the left-side hair over her left shoulder, out of the way for now.
steps.endState: The right side hangs separate.
steps.why: You are just keeping it out of the way while you work the right side first.

steps.title: Gather the right bunch
steps.instruction: Gather the right side and lift it level with the top of her right ear. Hold it firmly in your hand.
steps.endState: No loose strands on the right.

steps.title: Gather the left bunch
steps.instruction: Drop the left side off her shoulder. Gather it and lift it level with her left ear, holding both bundles at the same time to match.
steps.endState: Both bundles sit at the exact same height.

steps.title: Secure both bunches
steps.instruction: Wrap the first elastic round the right side at least three times. Then, repeat on the left side with a second elastic.
steps.endState: Neither side moves when she shakes her head.

steps.title: Check from the front
steps.instruction: Stand in front and compare. Level, and about the same thickness.
steps.withHer: Let her check them in the mirror.
steps.endState: Both bunches are equal in thickness when viewed from the front.

styles.name: Half-Up, Half-Down
styles.description: The top half of the hair gathered and tied high up on the back of her head; the bottom half left loose.
styles.herJob: She chooses what goes on top: a clip or an elastic.
styles.commonFailure: The top section looks thin because the dividing line was set too low.
styles.theFix: Undo the elastic and reset the dividing line. The tops of the ears are a reliable fixed marker. Go back to them and draw the line from there.

steps.title: Detangle all the hair
steps.instruction: Comb it all through before you split anything.
steps.endState: The comb runs freely everywhere.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, not dripping, and smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers. Work in sections, ends first, fingers then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section, root to tip.

steps.title: Find the dividing line
steps.instruction: Part the hair. Put your finger on the top of her right ear. Run the pointed end of the tail comb straight across the top of her head to her left ear.
steps.withHer: Ask her to keep her head level.
steps.endState: A clear parting line running from ear to ear.

steps.title: Gather the top section
steps.instruction: Gather the top half. Collect all the hair above that line with both hands. Use your fingers to press the remaining bottom half straight down to keep it out of the way.
steps.endState: All top hair is separated into one clean bundle.

steps.title: Smooth the sides
steps.instruction: Smooth the sides. Use a soft brush to sweep the hair above her forehead and ears neatly back toward your gathering hand.
steps.endState: The top and sides are pulled flat and bump-free.

curly.title: Smooth the sides
curly.instruction: Smooth the sides. Use your fingertips, not a brush, to sweep the hair above her forehead and ears neatly back toward your gathering hand.
curly.endState: The top and sides are smooth, with the curl pattern still intact.

steps.title: Secure high up on the back of her head
steps.instruction: Secure the ponytail. Hold the smoothed bundle firmly and loop an elastic around it at least three times. Position it high up on the back of her head.
steps.endState: The elastic sits snug and does not slide down.

curly.title: Secure high up on the back of her head
curly.instruction: Secure the ponytail. Hold the smoothed bundle firmly and loop an elastic around it at least three times, without dragging the parting line tight to get it there.
curly.endState: The elastic sits snug and does not slide down, with the parting line soft, not strained.

steps.title: Final polish
steps.instruction: Let the bottom half of her hair hang loose underneath, and smooth it down with your hand from behind her ears.
steps.endState: The join between the tied hair and loose hair looks clean and sharp

styles.name: Clip-Back for Baby Wisps
styles.description: Fine wisps clipped back from a baby or toddler's face using a single soft snap clip.
styles.herJob: She picks the clip.
styles.commonFailure: The clip pops open after a few minutes.
styles.theFix: Gather a slightly thicker section of wisps before clipping. The clip needs enough hair to grip. If the wisps are extremely fine, dampen them more thoroughly first.

steps.title: Dampen the wisps
steps.instruction: Run the comb under cold water, then draw it gently over the front hair only, from her forehead back about 5 cm.
steps.endState: Damp, not dripping wet.
steps.why: This settles fine baby hair enough to gather it.

curly.title: Dampen the wisps
curly.instruction: Dampen your fingertips, not a comb, and draw them gently over the front hair only, from her forehead back about 5 cm.
curly.endState: Damp, not dripping wet.

steps.title: Gather the wisps
steps.instruction: Sweep those wisps back off her forehead using your fingertips. Smooth them backward, but do not pull tightly toward the top.
steps.endState: Her face is clear and hair lies flat.
steps.why: You only want the front wisps, not the whole top section.

steps.title: Clip in place
steps.instruction: Slide a fabric-lined clip over the wisps, pointing front to back. Slide your finger underneath the clip as you snap it shut to protect her scalp.
steps.withHer: Let her choose the clip.
steps.endState: Secure, flat, and not pinching her skin.

styles.name: Twist-Back Sides
styles.description: The front hair on each side twisted back along the hairline and clipped above the ear. Made for chin-length hair, and for front hair that's growing out.
styles.oneLiner: Out of her eyes, all day
styles.herJob: She holds the second clip until you need it.
styles.commonFailure: The twist unwinds as soon as you let go.
styles.theFix: Twist further than looks necessary, and clip right at the end of the twist, not partway along it. On very silky hair, mist it first so it has some grip.

steps.title: Comb the front and sides
steps.instruction: Comb through the front and sides, from the hairline to the ends.
steps.endState: The comb runs from her hairline to the ends with no catching.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, not dripping, and smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers. Work in sections, ends first, fingers then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section, root to tip.

steps.title: Find her parting
steps.instruction: Use the parting she already has. If there isn't one, draw one with the pointed end of the tail comb from the middle of her hairline straight back, about two fingers' length.
steps.endState: A clear line runs back from the middle of her hairline.

curly.title: Find her parting
curly.instruction: Use the parting she already has. If there isn't one, draw one with the pointed end of the tail comb from the middle of her hairline straight back, about two fingers' length. Smooth the curls either side of it with your fingers.
curly.endState: A clear line runs back from the middle of her hairline, with the curls lying to either side.

steps.title: Take the first strip
steps.instruction: Stand in front of her. On her right side (your left), use the tail comb to take a strip of hair two fingers wide along her hairline, from the parting to just above her ear. Hold its end between your fingers.
steps.endState: One flat strip is lifted away from her hairline, and the rest of her hair hangs loose beneath it.

curly.title: Take the first strip
curly.instruction: Stand in front of her. On her right side (your left), use the tail comb to take a strip of curls two fingers wide along her hairline, from the parting to just above her ear. Mist it if it has dried, and hold its end between your fingers.
curly.endState: One strip of curls is lifted away from her hairline, and the rest hangs loose beneath it.

steps.title: Twist it back
steps.instruction: Turn the strip so it rolls back, away from her face, like turning a key, without adding any more hair. Keep turning until it is a firm rope lying against her head, running back towards the top of her ear.
steps.withHer: Ask her to keep her head still.
steps.endState: The rope lies along her hairline and stays twisted while you hold the end.

curly.title: Twist it back
curly.instruction: Split the strip into two halves and twist them round each other, away from her face, without adding any more hair. A two-strand twist holds on curly and coily hair where a single twist springs open.
curly.endState: A neat two-strand twist runs from the parting to above her ear.

steps.title: Clip it
steps.instruction: Hold the end of the rope just above her ear. Slide a snap clip over it, pointing towards the back of her head, catching a little of the hair underneath as well so the clip has something to grip. Keep one finger under the clip as you snap it shut.
steps.endState: The clip points back, lies flat and doesn't pinch, and the rope stays twisted when you let go.

curly.title: Clip it
curly.instruction: Hold the end of the twist just above her ear. Slide a snap clip over it, pointing towards the back of her head, catching a few curls underneath as well so the clip has something to grip. Keep one finger under the clip as you snap it shut.
curly.endState: The clip points back, lies flat and doesn't pinch, and the twist holds when you let go.

steps.title: Do the other side to match
steps.instruction: On her left side (your right), take the same strip, twist it back away from her face, and clip it at the same height with the second clip.
steps.endState: Seen from the front, both clips sit at the same height.

curly.title: Do the other side to match
curly.instruction: On her left side (your right), take the same strip, split it into two halves and twist them round each other, away from her face. Clip it at the same height with the second clip.
curly.endState: Seen from the front, both twists and both clips sit at the same height.

styles.name: Top Sprout
styles.description: The front and top hair gathered into one small ponytail on top of her head, so it stands up like a sprout. Made for very short hair and hair that's growing out.
styles.oneLiner: Tiny, and out of her eyes
styles.herJob: She holds the elastic ready on her finger.
styles.commonFailure: The short bits at the front slip out of the elastic.
styles.theFix: Gather from a little further forward, so the shortest hair at her hairline is in your hand before the elastic goes on. Mist the front first so short hair holds together.

steps.title: Mist the front and top
steps.instruction: Mist the front and top of her hair until it's damp, not dripping.
steps.endState: The hair feels damp and lies flat.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, not dripping, and smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers. Work in sections, ends first, fingers then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section, root to tip.

steps.title: Gather the top
steps.instruction: Put your fingertips at her hairline and comb the front and top hair back and up to the top of her head, between her forehead and her crown. Hold it in one hand.
steps.withHer: Ask her to tip her chin down.
steps.endState: All the hair from her hairline to the top of her head is in your hand.

curly.title: Gather the top
curly.instruction: Gather the front and top hair up to the top of her head with your fingertips, not the comb, without dragging at her hairline. Hold it in one hand.
curly.endState: All the hair from her hairline to the top of her head is in your hand, and her hairline is soft, not pulled.

steps.title: Wrap the elastic
steps.instruction: Wrap a mini elastic round the gathered hair two or three times, close to her head.
steps.endState: The sprout stands up on its own when you let go.

curly.title: Wrap the elastic
curly.instruction: Wrap a mini elastic round the gathered hair two or three times, close to her head.
curly.endState: The sprout sits up in a puff on its own when you let go.

steps.title: Check from the front
steps.instruction: Stand in front of her and look.
steps.endState: Her forehead is clear and the sprout sits in the middle.

styles.name: Side-Swept Clip
styles.description: The front hair swept across from a side parting and clipped flat above one ear. Made for short hair and a fringe that's growing out.
styles.oneLiner: One clip, out of her eyes
styles.herJob: She chooses which clip.
styles.commonFailure: The front hair springs back into her eyes.
styles.theFix: The clip is holding too little hair, or it sits too far forward. Take a little more of the front hair into the clip, and clip it just above her ear, not at her temple. On very silky hair, mist it first so it has some grip.

steps.title: Comb the front through
steps.instruction: Comb the front hair from her hairline to the ends.
steps.endState: The comb runs through with no catching.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, not dripping, and smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers. Work in sections, ends first, fingers then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section, root to tip.

steps.title: Make a side parting
steps.instruction: Use the pointed end of the tail comb to draw a parting on her left side, straight back from her hairline above the outer corner of her left eye, about two fingers' length.
steps.endState: A clear line runs back from her hairline on her left side.

steps.title: Sweep the front across
steps.instruction: With the comb, sweep the front hair from the parting across the top of her forehead towards her right ear.
steps.endState: The front hair lies flat across her forehead, clear of her eyes.

curly.title: Sweep the front across
curly.instruction: Sweep the front hair across towards her right ear with your fingertips, not the comb, so the curls keep their shape.
curly.endState: The curls lie across her forehead, clear of her eyes.

steps.title: Clip it above her ear
steps.instruction: Hold the swept hair just above her right ear. Slide a snap clip over it, catching a little of the hair underneath so it grips. Keep one finger under the clip as you snap it shut.
steps.withHer: Let her choose the clip.
steps.endState: The clip lies flat and doesn't pinch.

steps.title: Check from the front
steps.instruction: Stand in front of her and look.
steps.endState: Her eyes are clear and the clip doesn't show above her hairline.

styles.name: Two Little Sprouts
styles.description: The front and top hair parted down the middle and gathered into two small ponytails on top of her head, one either side of the parting. Made for very short hair and hair that's growing out.
styles.herJob: She checks in the mirror that they match.
styles.commonFailure: The two sprouts end up at different heights.
styles.theFix: Take the second one out. Feel where the first sits against the front of her right ear, find the same point against her left ear, and gather to it before the elastic goes on.

steps.title: Mist the front and top
steps.instruction: Mist the front and top of her hair until it's damp, not dripping.
steps.endState: The hair feels damp and lies flat.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, not dripping, and smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers. Work in sections, ends first, fingers then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section, root to tip.

steps.title: Part down the middle
steps.instruction: Run the pointed end of the tail comb from the middle of her hairline straight back to her crown.
steps.endState: A straight parting runs from her hairline to her crown, with the same amount of hair either side.

steps.title: Gather the first side
steps.instruction: Gather the hair on her right side of the parting, from her hairline back to her crown, with your fingertips. Bring it to a point on top of her head, a finger's width from the parting and in line with the front of her right ear. Hold it in one hand.
steps.endState: Everything on her right side, from her hairline to her crown, is in your hand, and the parting is still straight.

curly.title: Gather the first side
curly.instruction: Gather the hair on her right side of the parting up with your fingertips, without dragging at her hairline, to a point on top of her head, a finger's width from the parting and in line with the front of her right ear. Hold it in one hand.
curly.endState: Everything on her right side, from her hairline to her crown, is in your hand, and her hairline is soft, not pulled.

steps.title: Wrap the elastic
steps.instruction: Wrap a mini elastic round the gathered hair two or three times, close to her head.
steps.withHer: Ask her if it pulls anywhere.
steps.endState: The sprout stands up on its own when you let go.

curly.title: Wrap the elastic
curly.instruction: Wrap a mini elastic round the gathered hair two or three times, close to her head.
curly.endState: The sprout sits up in a puff on its own when you let go.

steps.title: Do the other side
steps.instruction: Gather her left side the same way, to the matching point in line with the front of her left ear, and wrap a mini elastic round it two or three times.
steps.endState: From the front, the two sprouts sit at the same height, the same distance from the parting, and neither pulls at her hairline.

styles.name: Loop Bun
styles.description: All her hair in one elastic, pulled only halfway through on the last loop and spread into a bun at the back of her head. No pins.
styles.herJob: She tells you how big the loop should be.

styles.name: Wrapped Ponytail
styles.description: A classic ponytail with the elastic hidden under a strip of her own hair, pinned out of sight. Neat enough for school photos.
styles.herJob: She checks in the mirror that the elastic has disappeared.

styles.name: Bedtime Pineapple
styles.description: Curly and coily hair gathered loosely high on her head at bedtime, under a satin bonnet, so her curls aren't flattened by the morning.
styles.herJob: She tips her head forward and holds it there while you gather.
styles.commonFailure: Her curls are flat at the back in the morning.
styles.theFix: The pineapple sat too far back, so she slept on it. Gather it further forward, right behind her hairline, and keep the scrunchie loose enough for two fingers. If her hair won't gather without pulling, or the scrunchie leaves a dent in her coils, skip the pineapple: the bonnet on its own, or a satin pillowcase, still keeps her curls.

steps.title: Refresh the curls
steps.instruction: Mist her curls lightly, just enough to soften them.
steps.endState: The curls feel soft and springy, not damp.

steps.title: Gather it high at the front
steps.instruction: Ask her to tip her head forward. Gather all her hair up with your fingertips, without combing it and without pulling at her edges, to the top of her head just behind her hairline.
steps.endState: All her hair is gathered loosely on top, just behind her hairline, the back of her neck is clear, and nothing pulls at her hairline.

steps.title: Loop the scrunchie once
steps.instruction: Loop a soft scrunchie, satin if you have one, round the gathered hair once, so it holds it loosely.
steps.endState: Two fingers slide under the scrunchie easily, and the curls above it fall forward towards her forehead.

steps.title: Put the bonnet on
steps.instruction: Put on a satin bonnet with a stretchy edge and no ties under her chin. Start at the back of her neck and draw it up and forward over the pineapple, so its edge sits behind her ears and along her hairline, snug but not tight, where it can't slip down over her face. A satin pillowcase does the same job without a bonnet.
steps.withHer: Ask her if the edge feels tight.
steps.endState: No curls show outside the bonnet, the pineapple inside isn't squashed flat, and the edge sits snug, not tight, clear of her face.

styles.name: Three-Strand Plait
styles.description: The classic braid: three equal sections crossed over each other alternately from the back of her neck to tip.
styles.oneLiner: The plait every other plait builds on
styles.herJob: She calls out Left, Middle, Right as you cross each strand.

steps.title: Detangle and gather at the back of her neck

styles.name: Plaited Pigtails
styles.description: Two three-strand plaits, one on each side of a centre parting.
styles.herJob: She holds the second elastic ready for her other side.

steps.title: Plait the right side to match

styles.name: Top Knot
styles.description: All hair gathered at the very top of her head, twisted into a rope, and wound around its own base to form a bun.
styles.herJob: She holds the bobby pins ready for the last step.

steps.title: Gather to the very top of her head
Twist the ponytail into a rope
Wind the rope around the base

styles.name: French Plait
styles.description: A three-strand plait that starts at the very top of her head and gathers in new hair from each side as it works toward the back of her neck, sitting flat against the head.
styles.herJob: She counts how many times you add in a new strip.

steps.title: Take a starting section at the very top of her head
Divide into three and do the opening cross
Add a strip on each side and cross over
Continue as a three-strand plait to the tip

styles.name: Dutch Plait
styles.description: Like a French plait, but each section crosses under the middle instead of over, creating a raised ridge that stands out from the head.
styles.herJob: She feels for the ridge and tells you when it appears.

steps.title: Take a starting section at the very top of her head
Divide into three and do the opening cross
Add a strip on each side and cross under

styles.name: Sports Bun
styles.description: A bun built to stay secure through a full match, using a double-anchored base, tight rope-winding, and perimeter pins.
styles.herJob: She keeps her water bottle capped and ready for after.

steps.title: Gather to the back of her head
Twist the ponytail into a tight rope
Wind the rope around the base
Secure with a second elastic at the base

styles.name: Bubble Ponytail
styles.description: A basic ponytail with elastics spaced evenly down its length, each gap pinched outward into a rounded bubble.
styles.herJob: She counts the bubbles as you make them.

styles.name: Puffs
styles.description: Hair gathered softly upward into one or two round, loosely secured puffs, shaped by hand rather than brushed smooth.
styles.herJob: She picks the scrunchie colours.

styles.name: Twisted Bunches
styles.description: Two low bunches, each twisted into a single rope and finished without a brush.
styles.herJob: She holds the end of the first twist while you start the second.

styles.name: Criss-Cross Bands
styles.description: Small bunches banded in rows and joined diagonally with their neighbours, building a crossed, lattice-like pattern down the head.
styles.herJob: She hands you one band at a time.

styles.name: Pull-Through Plait
styles.description: A column of small ponytails, each pulled through the gap in the one above it, that reads as one thick plait.
styles.oneLiner: Looks like a plait. Isn't one.
styles.herJob: She keeps the clip safe until you need it.

styles.name: Space Buns
styles.description: Two buns, one high on each side of her head, each built from a twisted ponytail wound round its own base and pinned.
styles.oneLiner: Two tidy knots, one each side.
styles.herJob: She holds the bobby pins ready for each side.

steps.title: Build the second bun to match

styles.name: Mini Top Knot
styles.description: The top section of her hair twisted into one small knot on top of her head, with the sides and back loose. Made for short hair.
styles.oneLiner: A little knot, all her own
styles.herJob: She tells you where on top it goes.

styles.name: Rope Ponytail
styles.description: A high ponytail split in two and twisted into a rope, so it stays tidy and out of the way through a match or a dance class.
styles.herJob: She counts the wraps out loud as you go down.

steps.title: Gather to the very top of her head

styles.name: Half-Up Bun
styles.description: The top half of her hair tied at her crown and wound into a small bun; the bottom half left loose.
styles.herJob: She chooses the elastic for the bun.

styles.name: Fishtail Plait
styles.description: Two halves of hair, with thin strips crossed from one half to the other, all the way down, to make a fishbone pattern.
styles.herJob: She calls out Left or Right before each cross.

steps.title: Detangle and gather at the back of her neck

techniques.title: Holding tension
techniques.description: The anchor hand, and why it matters more than the elastic
techniques.whyItMatters: Your free hand is the anchor. It rests flat against her head, between the section you're working and her scalp, for the whole time you're gathering or wrapping. The anchor hand is what controls the pull she feels: not the elastic, not how hard you tug the hair.
howToDoIt: Rest your free hand flat against her head, between the section you're working and her scalp, and keep it there the whole time you're gathering or wrapping.
Loop the elastic three times for an everyday style, or five or more for sport. Ask her how it feels after the third loop, before you add another.
howToCheck: Two fingers slide underneath the loop without forcing.
commonMistakes: Letting the elastic control the pull instead of your anchor hand. If she feels it snap into place rather than your hand holding steady, that's the elastic doing the work it shouldn't.
Assuming more loops is always safer. Extra loops make it tighter, not just more secure, so check how it feels before adding another.

techniques.title: Detangling without tears
techniques.description: Ends first, five centimetres at a time
techniques.whyItMatters: Starting at the roots drags every knot in the hair down into one tangle at the bottom, which is what turns detangling into a fight. Freshly washed hair is often the hardest to work through: the strands are clean and smooth, so the comb has nothing to grip and slides into knots instead of through them.
howToDoIt: Start the comb about five centimetres from the ends, not at the roots.
Work through the knots in that section until the comb runs free.
Move up five more centimetres and repeat, working your way up to the roots.
If freshly washed hair is fighting you, a light leave-in spray on damp hair, or waiting until the next morning, makes it easier to work through.
howToCheck: The comb passes through the last five centimetres without catching.
A comb run from root to tip in one smooth stroke without snagging.
commonMistakes: Starting at the roots instead of the ends, which drags every knot down into one tangle at the bottom.
Forcing the comb through a knot that's caught, rather than using short strokes on just that section. Forcing it pulls the knot tighter and pulls at her scalp.

techniques.title: Making a parting
techniques.description: Follow the bone, not your eye
techniques.whyItMatters: A line judged by eye tends to drift, because you're working from behind with no fixed point to check against. The centre seam of her skull is a real landmark you can feel with a fingertip, so following it gives a straighter line with far less guesswork, and it's in the same place every time.
howToDoIt: Feel for the centre seam of her skull with a fingertip before you commit the comb to it.
Run the comb's tail from her crown to her nape, following that seam rather than judging a straight line by eye.
If the line wanders, wet the comb and run it back along the same seam once.
howToCheck: Running a fingertip along the parting from front to back, it sits on the seam the whole way.
A parting that wanders half a centimetre, which is invisible to everyone but you.
commonMistakes: Judging the line by eye instead of feeling for the seam first. This is the single biggest reason a parting drifts off-centre.
Going over it more than once. One re-run with a wet comb is normal; chasing a perfectly straight line after that usually makes it worse, not better.

techniques.title: Choosing elastics
techniques.whyItMatters: Fabric-covered elastics grip the hair instead of the hair sliding inside them, and they don't leave the sharp crease a bare rubber band does. That crease is where hair fatigues and eventually breaks, so a fabric tie protects the hair as much as it holds the style.
howToDoIt: Choose a fabric-covered elastic over a bare rubber band.
Match the thickness to her hair: thinner ties for fine hair, which needs more wraps to hold at all; thicker ties for thick hair, which needs fewer.
Move the tie point slightly each time you can, rather than securing in exactly the same spot every day, so the wear spreads out instead of concentrating on one point of hair.
Keep a couple of spares in the kit. A snapped elastic mid-style is the only real emergency this app covers.
howToCheck: By the next morning, no hard crease left in the hair where the elastic sat.
The style held all day without needing a mid-day retie.
commonMistakes: Reaching for whatever elastic is in the drawer instead of matching it to her hair. The wrong thickness either won't hold or ends up over-tightened trying to make it hold.
Running out mid-style with no spare on hand, and having to stop and improvise.

techniques.title: Keeping her still
techniques.description: Give her a job, not an instruction
techniques.whyItMatters: Give her something to do with her hands and her eyes, rather than an instruction to sit still. A job works better than being told to stop moving, and a mirror facing her does two things at once: it lets her see what's happening, which lowers the sense of losing control, and it keeps her head still, because she stops turning around to look for you.
howToDoIt: Give her the spare clip to hold.
Ask her to count the wraps or the crosses out loud.
Angle a mirror so she can watch what's happening.
Work from slightly to her side rather than directly behind her, so you can reach either side without stepping around the chair.
howToCheck: She's occupied with her job rather than twisting round to check on you.
Her head stays roughly level without you needing to ask her to sit still.
commonMistakes: Repeating "sit still" or "stop moving". It rarely works twice in a row, and it turns the session into a battle instead of something she's part of.
Standing directly behind her, which makes it harder to check both sides match and means reaching round the chair every time.

techniques.title: Detangling curly and coily hair
techniques.description: Water and leave-in, not a dry brush
techniques.whyItMatters: Curly and coily hair tangles more easily and breaks more easily when it's dry. Brushing it dry is the fastest way to make her dread hair time. Water and leave-in are what make it painless.
howToDoIt: Mist her hair until it's damp, not dripping.
Smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers. On wash day, do this with conditioner still in.
Divide the hair into four sections and clip three away.
Start at the ends. Fingers first, then the wide-tooth comb, working up a little at a time.
Hold the hair just above any knot, so the pull lands on your hand, not her scalp.
When a section runs freely, twist it loosely out of the way and move to the next.
howToCheck: Your fingers slide through each section, root to tip.
She hasn't flinched since the first section.
commonMistakes: Starting at the roots. It pushes every small knot down into one big one.
Pulling harder at a knot. Add water and leave-in instead, then try again.
Doing the whole head at once. Small sections are quicker overall.

techniques.title: The two-strand twist
techniques.description: Two strands to keep track of, not three
techniques.whyItMatters: It's the simplest way to give curly and coily hair a style that holds for days, and it's easier than plaiting: two strands to keep track of, not three.
howToDoIt: Start on damp, detangled hair.
Take a section and split it into two equal strands.
Cross the right strand over the left, and keep going all the way down.
Keep the tension even. Firm enough to hold, never pulling at the root.
Twirl the end round your finger to finish.
On straight and wavy hair, twist each strand one way on its own, then wrap them round each other the opposite way, and band the end.
howToCheck: Run your fingers down it: it feels the same thickness from top to bottom.
It holds when you let go of the end.
commonMistakes: Uneven strands, which make a lopsided twist.
Twisting dry hair, which frizzes and unravels.
Twisting tight at the root to make it last. It won't last longer; it will just pull.

techniques.title: Gentle tension and protecting her edges
techniques.description: If it hurts, it's too tight
techniques.whyItMatters: Styles that pull too tight, done again and again, can damage the hair along her hairline over time. Dermatologists call it traction alopecia, and it's avoidable. The rule is simple: if it hurts, it's too tight.
howToDoIt: Use your anchor hand, as in Holding tension, so the elastic isn't doing the pulling.
Leave her hairline soft. Gather it; don't drag it back hard.
Use soft bands only, never ones with a metal join.
Lower and looser is kinder than high and tight.
Mix it up. Don't do the same tight style day after day, and give her hair rest days.
At night, a satin bonnet or pillowcase means less friction and fewer knots.
howToCheck: Two fingers slide under every band.
No bumps or redness along her hairline.
She says it feels fine, and you believed her.
commonMistakes: Redoing a style tighter so it lasts longer.
Ignoring an "ow" because you're nearly finished.
The same high ponytail every single morning.
techniques.note: If you notice broken hairs or thinning along her hairline, give her hair a rest from tight styles, and speak to your GP if it doesn't improve.

guides.name: Wash day
guides.description: Shampoo, conditioner, detangling and drying, in an order that keeps the knots down and the tears away.
guides.oneLiner: The knots come out in the conditioner, not the towel

parts.title: In the bath or shower
parts.when: Once or twice a week for straight and wavy hair; curly and coily hair usually once a week or less.

steps.title: Comb out the big knots first
steps.instruction: Before she gets in, comb her dry hair with the wide-tooth comb, starting at the ends and moving up to the roots only once the ends run free.
steps.endState: The comb passes from roots to ends in one stroke at the back, at both sides and at her crown.

curly.title: Loosen the big knots with your fingers
curly.instruction: Before she gets in, split her dry hair into four sections with your fingers and gently pull apart the biggest knots in each, ends first. Leave the comb for later, when the conditioner is in.
curly.endState: Each of the four sections separates easily in your fingers, with no knot bigger than a pea.

steps.title: Wet it right through
steps.instruction: Tip her head back with her chin up. Cup one hand along her hairline to keep the water out of her eyes, and pour warm water with the other, from her hairline back to her nape, until her hair is wet to the roots.
steps.withHer: Let her hold a dry flannel over her eyes.
steps.endState: When you squeeze a handful of hair at her crown, water runs out of it.

steps.title: Shampoo her scalp
steps.instruction: Rub a little shampoo, about the size of a large coin, between your palms and work it into her scalp with your fingertips: from her hairline, over her crown, down to her nape and behind both ears. Leave the lengths alone; the lather rinses down through them.
steps.withHer: Let her squeeze the shampoo into your palm.
steps.endState: There's lather across her whole scalp, including behind both ears and at her nape, and none worked into the ends.

curly.title: Shampoo her scalp
curly.instruction: Smooth a little shampoo, about the size of a large coin, onto her scalp only, pressing with flat fingertips in small circles: from her hairline, over her crown, down to her nape and behind both ears. Keep it off the lengths, which dry out easily.
curly.endState: There's shampoo across her whole scalp, including behind both ears and at her nape, and the lengths have none worked in.

steps.title: Rinse it all out
steps.instruction: With her head tipped back and your hand along her hairline again, rinse from her hairline to her nape until the water runs clear.
steps.endState: The water running off her nape is clear, with no bubbles in it.

steps.title: Conditioner on the lengths
steps.instruction: Smooth conditioner over her hair from the level of her ears down to the ends, with most on the ends. Keep it off her scalp.
steps.endState: Every strand below her ears feels slippery between your fingers.

curly.title: Plenty of conditioner, in sections
curly.instruction: Split her hair into four sections with your fingers. Smooth a generous handful of conditioner down each section from the roots to the ends, pressing it in between flat palms.
curly.endState: All four sections feel slippery right up to the scalp.

steps.title: Comb through the conditioner
steps.instruction: With the conditioner still in, comb one section at a time with the wide-tooth comb: the ends first, then from halfway, then from the roots. Move on when the comb runs through, and repeat round her whole head.
steps.endState: The comb passes from roots to ends in every section with no catching.
steps.why: Conditioner lets the comb slide, so the knots come out now rather than tearing on the towel.

curly.title: Detangle each section, still conditioned
curly.instruction: With the conditioner still in, take one section at a time: fingers first, then the wide-tooth comb, from the ends up to the roots. Twist each finished section loosely so it stays apart from the rest. Repeat for all four.
curly.endState: All four sections are detangled and twisted aside, and your fingers slide through each from roots to ends.

steps.title: Rinse the conditioner out
steps.instruction: Rinse from her hairline back to the ends, with your hand along her hairline, until the hair feels smooth but not slippery.
steps.endState: A section run between your fingers feels smooth, with no slippery coating left.

curly.title: Rinse most of it out
curly.instruction: Rinse with cool water from her hairline back, until most of the conditioner is out. A little left in helps curly and coily hair stay soft.
curly.endState: No white conditioner shows at her roots, and the hair still feels soft and slightly slippery.

parts.title: Drying
parts.when: Straight after the bath, before she gets cold.

steps.title: Squeeze, don't rub
steps.instruction: Wrap her hair in the towel and press it between your palms, working from her crown down to the ends. Keep the towel still rather than rubbing it back and forth.
steps.endState: Her hair is damp, not dripping: no drops fall from the ends when she stands up.

steps.title: Comb it into place
steps.instruction: Comb with the wide-tooth comb from the ends up, then lay it the way it falls, with her parting where she likes it.
steps.endState: The comb runs from roots to ends everywhere, and the hair lies flat at her crown.

curly.title: Leave-in, then leave it
curly.instruction: Smooth a little leave-in through each section with your fingers, from the roots to the ends, then leave the curls alone while they dry.
curly.endState: The curls are clumped together in ringlets or coils, not frizzed apart, and nothing has combed them since the leave-in.

steps.title: Dry it
steps.instruction: Let it air-dry, or use the dryer on warm, not hot. Keep it moving, about a hand's length from her head, and point it from her crown down toward the ends.
steps.withHer: Ask her if the air feels too hot.
steps.endState: Her scalp at the crown and behind her ears feels dry to your fingertips.

curly.title: Air-dry, or dry it from below
curly.instruction: Let it air-dry, or use the dryer on low and warm, held still below the curls and pointing up into them rather than blowing across them. Don't touch the curls while they dry.
curly.endState: Her scalp at the crown and behind her ears feels dry, and the curls still hold their shape.

notes: How often: straight and wavy hair usually once or twice a week, or when it looks greasy at the roots. Curly and coily hair usually once a week or less, with a rinse and conditioner in between if it needs it.
Shampoo in her eyes is what makes hair washing a battle. A dry flannel held over her eyes keeps them dry and gives her a job.
Never put her to bed with soaking hair: it tangles on the pillow. Damp is fine once it's combed through.
For a baby, warm water and a soft cloth are usually all the hair needs. Ask your health visitor or public health nurse if you're unsure.

suggestions.why: The same detangling, every morning between wash days.

guides.commonFailure: Combing the knots out of dry or freshly shampooed hair. It hurts, it snaps the hair, and the next wash day starts with tears.
guides.theFix: Stop, put conditioner on the knotted section, and work it from the ends with your fingers before the comb goes back in. The conditioner does the work. If a knot still won't give, leave it for the next wash day rather than pulling.

guides.name: Night and bonnets
guides.description: Brush out the day, plait or pineapple it loosely for sleep, and protect it with satin, so the morning starts without knots.
guides.oneLiner: A few minutes tonight saves a fight tomorrow

parts.title: Brushing out
parts.when: After her bath or before her story, while she's still awake enough to sit.

steps.title: Take everything out
steps.instruction: Take out everything from today's style. Slide each piece down along the hair and off, rather than pulling it straight out.
steps.endState: Run your hands over her whole head: there's nothing hard left in her hair.

steps.title: Brush out from the ends
steps.instruction: Brush one small section at a time from the ends, moving up only once the ends run free, until you reach the roots. Work round her whole head.
steps.withHer: Ask her to tell you when it pulls.
steps.endState: The brush passes from roots to ends in one stroke everywhere.

curly.title: Detangle with your fingers
curly.instruction: Mist one section at a time until it's damp, smooth a little leave-in through it, and separate the knots with your fingers, ends first. Leave the brush out at night.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through every section from roots to ends.

parts.title: Ready for sleep
parts.when: Last thing, once the hair is brushed out and dry or nearly dry.

steps.title: Gather it at her nape
steps.instruction: Gather all the hair loosely at her nape, the hollow at the back of her neck. Smooth it back from her hairline with your palm without pulling.
steps.endState: Every strand is in your hand, and she can nod without feeling a pull anywhere.

curly.title: Gather it high at the front
curly.instruction: Gather all her curls loosely with your fingertips toward the front of her head, to just behind her front hairline rather than on her crown, so she lies on the back of her head and not on her curls. This is the pineapple.
curly.endState: The curls sit loosely on top just behind her hairline, the back of her neck and her crown are clear, and nothing pulls at her hairline.

steps.title: Plait it loosely
steps.instruction: Split the gathered hair into three equal strands. Cross the right strand over the middle, then the left over the middle, without pulling, and repeat down the hair until there's about a finger's length left.
steps.endState: A loose plait runs down to a finger's length from the ends, and your fingertip slides between the strands.

curly.title: Hold the pineapple loosely
curly.instruction: Slip one soft scrunchie round the gathered curls and loop it over them once more, so it holds them without squeezing.
curly.endState: The scrunchie holds the curls just behind her hairline, the curls above it fall forward toward her forehead, and you can slide a finger under it easily.

steps.title: Tie the end softly
steps.instruction: Loop a soft scrunchie round the end of the plait, just enough to hold it.
steps.withHer: Let her choose the scrunchie.
steps.endState: The plait doesn't unravel when she shakes her head, and the scrunchie isn't tight on the hair.

curly.title: Check her edges
curly.instruction: Run your fingertips round her hairline, at her temples, above her ears and at her nape, feeling for any hair pulled tight toward the scrunchie.
curly.endState: Every bit of hair at her hairline lies relaxed, with nothing pulled tight.

steps.title: On with the satin
steps.instruction: Put the satin bonnet on from her forehead back, so the band sits on her hairline and all her hair is inside. Or, if she won't wear one, put a satin pillowcase on her pillow.
steps.endState: All her hair is inside the bonnet, its band lies flat along her hairline, and nothing presses on her ears; or her pillow is in the satin case.
steps.why: Satin lets the hair slide as she turns in her sleep, so it doesn't rub into knots or frizz.

parts.title: Ready for sleep: under three
parts.when: Last thing, once the hair is brushed out and dry or nearly dry.

steps.title: Leave it loose
steps.instruction: Leave her hair loose for sleep, with nothing tied or clipped in it. Run your fingertips over her whole head, from her hairline to her nape.
steps.endState: Her hair hangs loose, and your fingertips find nothing in it anywhere from her hairline to her nape.
steps.why: Under three, anything small left in her hair is a choking risk in bed.

steps.title: Satin on her pillow
steps.instruction: Put a satin pillowcase on her pillow, or a satin bonnet on her from her forehead back, with all her hair inside.
steps.endState: Her pillow is in the satin case; or all her hair is inside the bonnet and nothing presses on her ears.
steps.why: Satin lets the hair slide as she turns in her sleep, so it doesn't rub into knots.

notes: Under three, sleep has a part of its own: her hair left loose, with nothing tied or clipped in it, and nothing on her head or pillow for a baby. If her hair is long enough to knot overnight, a loose plait with the end left untied is fine. The sleep note below says why.
Dry it first. Hair that goes to bed soaking wet tangles on the pillow; damp and combed through is fine.
A satin bonnet is the easiest win for curly and coily hair. A satin pillowcase does the same job for a child who pulls a bonnet off in her sleep.

suggestions.why: The loose plait for sleep, written out step by step.
The pineapple, step by step, for curly and coily hair.
Two plaits: less to lie on than one.

guides.commonFailure: A plait or pineapple tied too tightly to sleep in, so it pulls all night and she wakes up sore.
guides.theFix: Take the scrunchie off and redo it looser: you should be able to slide a finger under the band and between the strands. A sleep style only has to stop the tangles; it doesn't have to look neat.

guides.name: Swim day
guides.description: Wet it with clean water first, a style that stays put under the cap, and the pool rinsed out before it dries.
guides.oneLiner: Clean water in first means less pool water soaks in

parts.title: Before the lesson
parts.when: At home, or in the changing room before she gets in.

steps.title: Wet it with clean water
steps.instruction: Before she goes near the pool, wet her hair right through under the shower, from her hairline back to her nape.
steps.endState: When you squeeze a handful of hair at her crown, water runs out of it.
steps.why: Hair already full of clean water soaks up less of the pool water.

steps.title: Leave-in on the lengths
steps.instruction: Smooth a little leave-in through the wet lengths with your fingers, from the level of her ears down to the ends.
steps.endState: The hair feels slippery from ear level to the ends.

steps.title: One plait from her nape
steps.instruction: Comb it back with the wide-tooth comb, gather it at her nape, and plait it down to the ends: right strand over the middle, then left over the middle, repeated until a finger's length is left.
steps.withHer: Ask her to tip her chin down.
steps.endState: One plait hangs from her nape, and there's no loose hair at her ears or her neck.

curly.title: Two plaits behind her ears
curly.instruction: Split the hair down the middle with your fingers and plait each side from just behind her ear down to the ends: right over the middle, left over the middle, until a finger's length is left.
curly.endState: Two plaits start just behind her ears and lie flat, with nothing loose at her hairline.

steps.title: Tie the end
steps.instruction: Wrap a snag-free elastic round the end of the plait until it holds.
steps.endState: The plait doesn't loosen when she shakes her head.

curly.title: Tie both ends
curly.instruction: Wrap a snag-free elastic round the end of each plait until it holds.
curly.endState: Neither plait loosens when she shakes her head.

steps.title: Cap on, front to back
steps.instruction: Stretch the cap open between both hands, set its front edge on her forehead at the hairline, and roll it back over her crown and down past her nape, tucking the plait inside.
steps.withHer: Ask her if the cap pinches her ears.
steps.endState: The cap's edge runs from her hairline, over the tops of her ears, to below the plait at her nape, with no hair showing.

curly.title: Cap on, front to back
curly.instruction: Stretch the cap open between both hands, set its front edge on her forehead at the hairline, and roll it back over her crown and down past her nape, folding both plaits up inside it.
curly.endState: The cap's edge runs from her hairline, over the tops of her ears, to her nape, with both plaits inside and no hair showing.

parts.title: After the lesson
parts.when: In the changing room, straight after she gets out.

steps.title: Cap off from the back
steps.instruction: Lift the cap away from her nape first and roll it forward over her crown to her forehead.
steps.endState: The cap is off and the plait is still in.

steps.title: Rinse the pool out
steps.instruction: Under the changing-room shower, rinse her hair with the plait still in, from her hairline back to the ends, until it smells of water rather than the pool.
steps.withHer: Ask her to tip her head back.
steps.endState: A handful of hair by her ear smells of nothing but water.

steps.title: Undo the plait
steps.instruction: Slide the elastic off and undo the plait with your fingers, from the end up.
steps.endState: All the hair hangs loose, with no twists left in it.

curly.title: Undo both plaits
curly.instruction: Slide each elastic off and undo each plait with your fingers, from the end up.
curly.endState: All the hair hangs loose, with no twists left in either side.

steps.title: Leave-in through
steps.instruction: Smooth a little leave-in through the lengths with your fingers, from the level of her ears to the ends.
steps.endState: The lengths feel slippery from ear level to the ends.

steps.title: Comb from the ends
steps.instruction: Comb with the wide-tooth comb, the ends first, then from halfway, then from the roots, round her whole head.
steps.endState: The comb passes from roots to ends everywhere with no catching.

curly.title: Detangle in sections
curly.instruction: Split the hair into four sections with your fingers. In each, work out the knots with your fingers first, then the wide-tooth comb, from the ends up to the roots.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each of the four sections from roots to ends.

parts.title: Once a week
parts.when: On wash day, in a week she has swum.

steps.title: Clarifying shampoo on her scalp
steps.instruction: In place of her usual shampoo, work a little clarifying shampoo into her wet scalp with your fingertips, from her hairline over her crown to her nape and behind both ears.
steps.endState: There's lather across her whole scalp, including behind both ears.
steps.why: Clarifying shampoo lifts the build-up of pool water that her usual shampoo leaves behind.

steps.title: Rinse it through the lengths
steps.instruction: Rinse from her hairline back, letting the lather run down through the lengths, until the water runs clear.
steps.endState: The water off her nape is clear and her hair smells of nothing but water.

steps.title: Conditioner, and comb through
steps.instruction: Smooth her usual conditioner over the lengths and comb it through with the wide-tooth comb from the ends up, then rinse.
steps.endState: The comb ran through every section before you rinsed, and her hair feels soft, not squeaky.

curly.title: Plenty of conditioner, in sections
curly.instruction: Smooth a generous handful of conditioner through each of four sections from roots to ends, detangle each with your fingers and then the wide-tooth comb, and rinse most of it out.
curly.endState: Each section was detangled before rinsing, and her hair feels soft and slightly slippery.

notes: Curly and coily hair: clarify every other week rather than every week, and always follow it with plenty of conditioner.
Fair hair can take on a green tinge after a lot of lessons. The rinse after every lesson and the weekly clarifying wash are what stop it.
No time after the lesson? Rinse it, at least. Pool water left to dry in the hair is what does the damage.

suggestions.why: One plait from her nape: it fits under a cap.
Two plaits that last the lesson and the journey home.
A low bun under the cap, for hair well past her shoulders.

guides.commonFailure: Pool water left to dry in her hair, so it's dry, tangled and smelling of the pool by the evening.
guides.theFix: Rinse it in the changing room every time, even with no time for anything else, and comb it with leave-in before bed. If it's already dry and matted, do wash day's conditioner and comb steps that evening.

guides.name: Sport and PE day
guides.description: Hair fully off her face and secure for running, contact and tumbling, a low style that sits comfortably under a helmet, and a gentle take-down afterwards.

parts.title: Off her face and secure
parts.when: Before a PE lesson, a match, training or gymnastics.

steps.title: Brush it smooth
steps.instruction: Brush from the ends up until the brush passes from roots to ends everywhere.
steps.endState: The brush runs through in one stroke at the back, both sides and her crown.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, smooth a little leave-in through with your fingers, and work through in sections, ends first: fingers, then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section from roots to ends.

steps.title: Gather it low
steps.instruction: Smooth all the hair back from her hairline with your palm and gather it at the back of her head, level with the bottoms of her ears, so nothing sits high enough to press when she lies on her back.
steps.withHer: Ask her to look straight ahead.
steps.endState: No hair is left at her face or temples, and the gathered hair sits level with the bottoms of her ears.

curly.title: Gather it low
curly.instruction: Smooth the hair back from her hairline with damp fingertips and gather it at the back of her head, level with the bottoms of her ears, so nothing sits high enough to press when she lies on her back.
curly.endState: No hair is left at her face or temples, and the gathered hair sits level with the bottoms of her ears.

steps.title: Two elastics, not one
steps.instruction: Wrap a snag-free elastic round the gathered hair until it holds firmly, then wrap a second elastic a finger's width below it.
steps.withHer: Ask her if it pulls anywhere.
steps.endState: The ponytail doesn't shift when she shakes her head hard or jumps on the spot.
steps.why: Two elastics share the pull, so one can loosen without the whole style falling out mid-match.

steps.title: Plait the tail
steps.instruction: Plait the ponytail down to the ends, right over the middle, then left over the middle, until a finger's length is left, and tie the end with a third elastic.
steps.endState: A tied plait hangs from the elastics, so the hair can't whip across her face or a teammate's.

steps.title: Headband for the short hairs
steps.instruction: Slide a soft sports headband up from the back of her neck and over her hairline, so it catches the short hairs at her forehead and temples.
steps.endState: No hair falls into her eyes when she bends forward and stands back up.

parts.title: Under a helmet
parts.when: Camogie, hurling, cycling, horse riding: anything with a helmet.

steps.title: Split it down the middle
steps.instruction: Comb it back with the wide-tooth comb, then split it into two halves down the middle with your fingers, from her forehead to her nape.
steps.endState: Two equal halves, one over each shoulder, with a line down the middle of her head.

steps.title: A low plait each side
steps.instruction: Plait each half from just below her ear down to the ends: right over the middle, then left over the middle, until a finger's length is left.
steps.endState: Two plaits start below her ears and hang down, and the back of her head is smooth under your palm.
steps.why: The back of a helmet sits on the back of her head. Plaits that start below her ears sit under it rather than pressing into it.

steps.title: Tie the ends, nothing hard
steps.instruction: Wrap a snag-free elastic round the end of each plait: no beads, no metal and nothing chunky.
steps.endState: Run your palm over the back of her head and down each plait: nothing hard anywhere.

steps.title: Helmet on, and feel the back
steps.instruction: Put the helmet on and fasten it as its instructions say. Then slide two fingers inside the back of the helmet and feel along her head for anything pressing.
steps.withHer: Ask her if anything presses at the back.
steps.endState: The helmet sits level, both plaits come out below it, and your fingers find nothing pressing on the back of her head.

steps.title: Take it down gently
steps.instruction: Slide each elastic down along the hair and off, then undo the plaits with your fingers from the ends up.
steps.endState: All the hair hangs loose, with every elastic out and no hair pulled out with them.

steps.title: Freshen the roots
steps.instruction: Mist her roots with water and rub them gently with your fingertips, from her hairline over her crown to her nape, then let them dry.
steps.endState: Her roots feel fresh and dry, not damp and sticky.
steps.why: A wet rub lifts the sweat without a full wash. After a very muddy match, do wash day instead.

steps.title: Brush it out
steps.instruction: Brush from the ends up until the brush passes from roots to ends everywhere.
steps.endState: The brush runs through in one stroke at the back, both sides and her crown.

curly.title: Detangle with your fingers
curly.instruction: Smooth a little leave-in through each section and separate the knots with your fingers, ends first, then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section from roots to ends.

notes: No clips or pins for contact sport, gymnastics or tumbling: anything hard can dig in during a tackle or a fall. Elastics and a soft headband only.
Put a spare elastic or two in her sports bag. One often snaps mid-match.

Camogie and hurling players wear helmets for matches and training, and so do cyclists and riders. The helmet's fit is for her coach and the helmet's instructions; this routine is only about the hair underneath it.
Not so tight it hurts. A ponytail for sport has to stay put, but she should still be able to raise her eyebrows without feeling a pull.

suggestions.why: A secure bun for running and tumbling, without a helmet.
Lies flat to her head and holds through a whole match.
The two low plaits, written out step by step.

guides.commonFailure: A bun or a high ponytail that presses into the back of her head under a helmet, or bumps when she lies on her back.
guides.theFix: Take it down and redo it as two low plaits that start below her ears. Check with your palm: the back of her head should feel smooth, with nothing hard on it.

guides.name: Dance and drama day
guides.description: A neat, secure bun for ballet and dance, a show version that lasts a long evening under lights, a base for Irish dancing, and hair off her face for drama.
guides.oneLiner: Pins point along the bun, never into her head

parts.title: A ballet bun
parts.when: Before a ballet or dance class.

steps.title: Brush it, then mist it
steps.instruction: Brush from the ends up until it runs through, then mist it lightly all over so the hair holds together.
steps.endState: The brush runs from roots to ends everywhere, and the hair is just damp, not wet.

curly.title: Detangle it damp
curly.instruction: Mist her hair until it's damp, smooth leave-in through with your fingers, and detangle in sections, ends first: fingers, then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through each section from roots to ends.

steps.title: Gather it level with her ears
steps.instruction: Brush all the hair back from her hairline and up from her nape to a point at the back of her head level with the tops of her ears.
steps.withHer: Ask her to tip her chin down slightly.
steps.endState: No hair is left at her face or her neck, and the gathered hair sits level with the tops of her ears.

curly.title: Gather it level with her ears
curly.instruction: Smooth the hair back from her hairline and up from her nape with damp palms and a little leave-in, then smooth the surface with the soft-bristle brush, and gather it at the back of her head level with the tops of her ears.
curly.endState: No hair is left at her face or her neck, and the gathered hair sits level with the tops of her ears.

steps.title: Secure the ponytail
steps.instruction: Wrap a snag-free elastic round the gathered hair until it holds firmly.
steps.endState: The ponytail doesn't move when she nods, and she can raise her eyebrows without feeling a pull.
steps.why: Raising her eyebrows tests the tension at her hairline. If she feels it there, she'll feel it all through class.

steps.title: Twist and coil
steps.instruction: Twist the ponytail into a rope, then coil it round the elastic and tuck the end under the coil.
steps.endState: A round, flat bun covers the elastic, with the end hidden underneath.

steps.title: Pin along the bun
steps.instruction: Push a bun pin in at the outer edge of the bun, pointing along the coil toward its middle, catching the bun and a little hair beneath it. Never point a pin into her scalp. Repeat round the bun with three or four pins.
steps.withHer: Ask her if any pin digs in.
steps.endState: The bun stays still when you push it gently, and she says nothing is digging in.
steps.why: A pin pushed along the coil grips the hair; one pushed inward only scratches her head.

steps.title: Net over the bun
steps.instruction: Most ballet classes ask for a hair net. Stretch it over the bun and wind the spare net round it until it's snug.
steps.endState: The net covers the whole bun with no hair poking out of it.

parts.title: For a show
parts.when: On top of the bun, for a performance or a long evening under lights.

steps.title: Smooth the flyaways
steps.instruction: Mist the soft-bristle brush lightly and brush it over her hairline and the top of her head toward the bun.
steps.endState: In a mirror, no short hairs stand up along her hairline or at her crown.

curly.title: Smooth the edges
curly.instruction: Smooth a little leave-in over her hairline and the top of her head with your fingertips, toward the bun, then go over it once with the soft-bristle brush.
curly.endState: In a mirror, her hairline and crown look smooth, with no hair standing up.

steps.title: One more pin each side
steps.instruction: Push one more bun pin into each side of the bun, pointing along the coil, never into her scalp.
steps.endState: The bun stays put when she shakes her head, and nothing digs in.

steps.title: Try a costume change
steps.instruction: Have her pull a top over her head and put on any hat or headpiece she'll wear, then look at the bun.
steps.withHer: Let her do the costume change herself.
steps.endState: After the change the bun is still in place, and the headpiece sits on it without pushing the pins in.

parts.title: Irish dancing
parts.when: The base for a competition wig or curls, for a feis or a show.

steps.title: Gather it at her crown
steps.instruction: Brush all the hair up from her hairline and her nape to her crown, the highest point of her head.
steps.endState: No hair is left at her face or her neck, and it's gathered at the very top of her head.

curly.title: Gather it at her crown
curly.instruction: Smooth the hair up from her hairline and her nape with damp palms and a little leave-in, and gather it at her crown, the highest point of her head.
curly.endState: No hair is left at her face or her neck, and it's gathered at the very top of her head.

steps.title: Secure it
steps.instruction: Wrap a snag-free elastic round the gathered hair until it holds firmly.
steps.endState: The ponytail doesn't move when she nods, and she can raise her eyebrows without feeling a pull.

steps.title: A flat bun
steps.instruction: Twist the ponytail into a rope, coil it flat round the elastic, and tuck the end under.
steps.endState: A flat bun sits at her crown, with no lump that would lift a wig.

steps.title: Pin it flat
steps.instruction: Push bun pins in at the outer edge of the bun, pointing along the coil toward the middle, never into her scalp, until it doesn't move.
steps.endState: The bun is flat and still when you press it, and nothing digs in.

steps.title: Wig on, her teacher's way
steps.instruction: Put the wig or curls on over the bun and fasten them the way her dance school shows you. Then have her turn her head from side to side.
steps.withHer: Ask her if the wig pulls anywhere.
steps.endState: The wig sits evenly on the bun without a bump, and it doesn't shift or pull when she turns her head.

parts.title: Drama
parts.when: A rehearsal or a play, with changes between scenes.

steps.title: Lift the front section
steps.instruction: Gather the hair from both temples and the top of her head back to her crown, leaving the rest hanging.
steps.endState: Her face is clear from the front and both sides, and the hair below her ears hangs loose.

steps.title: Tie it with a scrunchie
steps.instruction: Loop a soft scrunchie round the gathered hair at the back of her head until it holds.
steps.endState: The section stays put when she pulls a top over her head, and the scrunchie hasn't moved.

steps.title: Count the pins out
steps.instruction: Feel for every bun pin and slide each one out the way it went in, counting them against the number you put in.
steps.withHer: Let her count the pins with you.
steps.endState: You've counted out as many pins as went in.

steps.title: Net and elastic off
steps.instruction: Take the hair net off, unwind the bun, and slide the elastic down along the hair and off.
steps.endState: The hair hangs loose, with nothing left in it.

steps.title: Brush out gently
steps.instruction: Brush from the ends up until it runs from roots to ends everywhere.
steps.endState: The brush passes through in one stroke everywhere, and she says her head feels fine.

curly.title: Detangle with your fingers
curly.instruction: Smooth a little leave-in through each section and separate it with your fingers, ends first, then the wide-tooth comb.
curly.endState: Your fingers slide through every section from roots to ends.

notes: Not so tight it hurts. Through a long rehearsal she should be able to raise her eyebrows and nod without a pull. A headache after class means it was too tight.
Ask her class what they want: some ask for a net, some for a particular height of bun, some for nothing in the hair at all.
Irish dancing wigs and curls: her teacher or dance school will show you how they want them fixed for a feis. This routine stops at the bun underneath, which is the part you can always do.
For a show, pack spare bun pins, an elastic and the hair net in her costume bag.

suggestions.why: A high bun, for a class that wants one.
A quick bun for drama and changes between scenes.

guides.commonFailure: A bun pinned so tightly, or with pins pushed inward, that she has a headache by the interval.
guides.theFix: Take the pins out and redo the ponytail a little looser, then pin along the bun rather than into it. Fewer pins, placed along the coil, hold better than many pushed straight in.

guides.name: Nits day
